title: MAGE: A Multi-Agent Engine for Automated RTL Code Generation
problem: Single-LLM RTL generation approaches fail to produce syntactically and functionally correct Verilog due to the complexity of navigating multiple languages and handling generation, verification, and correction tasks simultaneously.
motivation: Automated RTL generation from natural language enables faster hardware design, but single agents cannot reliably handle correctness guarantees.
method: MAGE uses multiple AI agents working together to generate Verilog code. The system generates many diverse candidates by using high-temperature sampling (varying how randomly the AI makes choices to explore more options). It immediately tests each candidate and catches functional errors, providing precise feedback about what broke. Agents then iteratively refine the code based on this feedback until it works correctly.
key_novelty: Multiple AI agents with immediate code testing catch bugs in generated Verilog earlier.
contributions: High-temperature RTL candidate sampling exploring diverse code space
Verilog-state checkpoint checking enabling early functional error detection
Multi-agent coordination for generation, verification, and targeted debugging
95.7% syntactic and functional correctness on VerilogEval-Human v2; 23.3% improvement over Claude-3.5-sonnet

metrics.accuracy: 95.7% syntactic and functional correctness; 23.3% improvement over SOTA

limitations: Not discussed—focus on benchmark results without discussing design complexity limits or scalability.
primary_theme: Multi-agent LLM system for correct Verilog RTL generation
